info.name: Pristoria
info.description: Four new races based on different Dinosaurs

description.p: Deep underground, even deeper than the Underdark, lies a city as prehistoric as the Weave itself. A civilization made of four races, the Pristoria, living together in a war they call harmonic. Ankylon are one of these races. Easy-going, taking their life slow and gentle.

Ankylon strive from piece. They do not enjoy conflict, and they don't have many that could harm them underground. Despite that, if threatened, they do not hold back on protecting themselves. Ankylon mostly eat plants, allthough they learned to like the honey that is produced by one of the very few bees that live by the flower fields at the towns center.

An Ankylons body is protected my big, hard as bone plates along their back. These plates protect them from injury in such a well manner that they have no known predators, as any predator wouldn't get to their meat even if an Ankylon died. To top it all off, Ankylon are adorned with a tail that holds a club like Bone at its end that it can use to attack any attacker.

Ankylon share some gender specific differences, hence why part of their name is often influenced by exactly those. Male Ankylon all have very similar back plates, but their tail club may come in many shapes. One could have a perfect sphere as a club, another could have a more janky one whilst yet another may have small spikes growing around it. Female Ankylon on the other hand have generally generic tail clubs, but their back plates are unique. Some may have oval shaped plated while another could have two plates grow together to resemble something like hearts.
Your Ankylon character has the following racial traits.
Ability Score Increase. Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Strength score increases by 1.
Age. Ankylon mature and age at about the same rate as humans. In some rare cases, they may exceed the age of 100.
Alignment. Ankylon are inclined toward good neutrality. They dislike fights, but aren't afraid to protect themselves when attacked.
Size. Ankylon stand between 8 and 9 feet tall. Your size is Medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.
Plated. Your body is covered in hard Scute-like plates. While you're wearing no armor, your AC equals 13 + your Constitution modifier. You still benefit from the effect of Shields.

Club. Your tail club counts as a natural melee weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

Denting. Your tail club can be devastating to your opponents armor. When you land a critical hit with your tail club and the creature you hit is wearing armor, you dent it. A creature with dented armor recieves a -1 penalty to their AC until the end of your next turn.
Strong Build. You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push or drag.
Survivor. You have proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Medicine, Nature, or Survival.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and Pristorian. Pristorian is widely spoken in the Cave cities of the Pristorian races, for it is ancient, more so than common ever was.

Your Cephalo character has the following racial traits.
Ability Score Increase. Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Strength score increases by 1.
Age. Cephalo mature at about the same rate as humans. They live for up to 75 years.

Alignment. Cephalo are inclined toward chaotic neutrality. They dislike fights in general, but they also get a rise out of annoying others with witty comments are heabutts that aren't hard enough to hurt but hard enough to annoy.
Size. Cephalo stand at around 7 feet tall. Your size is Medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 40 feet.

Dome. Your hardned head dome counts as a natural melee weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with it, you deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

Headbutt Rush. After moving 20 feet in a straight line, if you hit a creature with your Dome, you push them forwards. The creature makes a strength saving throw, on a failed save, the creature gets pushed 5 feet backwards. If the creature hits a solid surface or another creature, both receive an additional 1d12 bludgeoning damage.
Quick Build. Your movement speed is 40. Additionally, once per long rest, you can use the dash action as a bonus action.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and Pristorian. Pristorian is widely spoken in the Cave cities of the Pristorian races, for it is ancient, more so than common ever was.

setters.set: Male Cephalo are often named after the arrangement of horns behind their head dome.
Female Cephalo are often called after the curvature of their head dome.

Your Tricera character has the following racial traits.
Ability Score Increase. Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Strength score increases by 1.
Age. Tricera mature at about the same rate as humans. They live for up to 60 years.
Alignment. Tricera are inclined toward good neutrality. They dislike fights, but their temper often leads to misunderstandings that causes them to act out of defensiveness.
Size. Tricera stand at around 8 feet tall. Your size is Medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Frilled Guard. Your shield-like head helps you survive against especially harsh blows. When a creature you can see hits you with a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to gain a +3 bonus to your AC on that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss instead. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain expended uses after finishing a Long Rest.

Horns. The horns on your head count as a natural melee weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

Stampede Rush. After moving 20 feet in a straight line, if you hit a creature with your Horn, you make them tumble, potentially falling down. The creature makes a strength saving throw, gaining the prone condition on a failed save.
Strong Build. You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push or drag.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and Pristorian. Pristorian is widely spoken in the Cave cities of the Pristorian races, for it is ancient, more so than common ever was.

Your Amargan character has the following racial traits.
Ability Score Increase. Your Strength score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 1.
Age. Amargan mature and age at about the same rate as humans.
Alignment. Amargan are inclined toward neutrality. They enjoy their personal space and respect the ones of others. They are very territorial and not afraid to keep their space to themselves.
Size. Amargan stand between 8 and 9 feet tall. Your size is Medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Spined Neck. Your spined neck counts as a natural melee weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike. Your range for this natural weapon is 10 feet.

Wary Spines. You've grown wary of foes approaching into your personal space. When a creature you can see enters your natural weapon's reach, you can use your reaction to make an attack of opportunity against the invading creature.
Strong Build. You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push or drag.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and Pristorian. Pristorian is widely spoken in the Cave cities of the Pristorian races, for it is ancient, more so than common ever was.
